heard: Sunlight feels instant, but its energy spent 100,000 years escaping the core. When nuclear fusion occurs deep inside the sun, it releases tiny light particles called photons. These photons bounce constantly between dense particles in an epic and incredibly long obstacle course. At the very same exact time, nuclear reactions also release nearly massless ghost particles called neutrinos. Because they interact so weakly with normal matter, neutrinos escape the dense core right away. Detecting those mysterious neutrinos, today proved the sun produces the same energy now as it did long ago. Sunlight hitting your face today is actually an ancient relic spent escaping the core.
